question.problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ k \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$
question.worked_solution:
If $b\in \text{Null}(A),$ then we must have $Ab=0.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ k \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2k+2 \\ 4k-4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2k+2=0 \\ 4k-4=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=1.$
